## See Cloudflare Workers Builds

- Workers that deploy from git (Workers Builds) now show the build while it runs, then **Ready** or **Failed**, with the branch, commit and message. Before, a push only showed up once it was already live, as "Deployed with wrangler".
- A push notifies once. The wrangler deploy that a build runs for you is folded into the build; a wrangler deploy of your own after the build still shows on its own.
- Builds from non-production branches count as previews, like Pages and Vercel previews.
- Add **Workers Builds Configuration: Read** to your Cloudflare token to turn this on (edit it at dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens; the token itself doesn't change). Without it, Workers show exactly as before.

## Tell Workers and Pages apart

- A Cloudflare account can have a Worker and a Pages project with the same name. Settings used to show them as two identical rows; each Cloudflare project now says **Worker** or **Pages** next to its last deploy.
- VoiceOver reads the kind with the project name too, so the two toggles no longer sound the same.

## Better signals, without your project data

- Measure whether project filters, collapse controls, and bulk selection help people navigate large accounts, so future improvements follow actual feature use.
- Measure manual update checks and changes to the automatic-update preference to improve update discoverability.
- Keep daily active use separate from an app merely running in the background, using anonymous installation counts rather than claiming to count people.

## Privacy stays in your control

- These additions use explicit user actions, not automatic screen tracking, session replay, or per-keystroke capture.
- Search text, account/group identities, project names, repositories, deployment content, tokens, URLs, and error messages are never sent. Bulk-selection counts use coarse ranges.
- Analytics remains optional and on by default in configured release builds. Turn off **Share usage analytics** in **Settings → General → Privacy** at any time. Existing opt-outs are preserved.
- The privacy page now explains the additional feature-usage signals: https://deployedyet.com/privacy.

## Find the deployment you need
- Search tracked deployments by project, team, account, branch, commit, message or provider. Press Cmd+F to jump to search.
- Combine provider and deployment-state filters, see matching counts, and clear everything in one click. Monitoring warnings and failure headlines remain visible even when a filter hides the affected row.

## Keep large accounts manageable
- Collapse individual project groups in Account Settings, or use Collapse All / Expand All. Your layout is remembered separately for each account.
- Search temporarily opens matching groups. Clearing search restores your saved layout, and bulk selection changes only matching projects.
- Group controls include explicit selection scope and accessible expanded/collapsed state.

## Optional, privacy-focused usage analytics
- Limited usage analytics helps measure daily active installations and improve features. It is on by default in this release, with an immediate opt-out notice and an always-available switch in Settings → General → Privacy. Collection can begin before the notice is dismissed; existing explicit opt-outs are preserved.
- Events use a random installation identifier and coarse usage properties. They never include provider tokens, account labels, project names or IDs, repositories, paths, URLs, branches, commit messages or error text. No session replay, automatic screen capture or crash reporting.
- Turning it off cancels pending collection and clears the local analytics identity and queued events. It cannot retract events already received. PostHog receives your network address on connection, although the app suppresses IP properties and disables location enrichment. Read the updated privacy page at https://deployedyet.com/privacy.

## Know when monitoring needs attention

- See a visible monitoring warning when a provider, team, or repository cannot be checked, instead of mistaking cached deployments for a fresh all-clear.
- Keep your cached deployment rows during provider outages, with an honest last-successful-full-check timestamp in Settings.
- Refresh performs a full check, clears warnings after recovery, and respects the existing rate-limit cooldown even when only part of an account fails.
- GitHub discovery and newly discovered repository polling now preserve rate-limit responses too.
- Recent failed deployments keep headline priority so monitoring warnings do not hide a broken deploy.
